key_insight: A reinforcement-learning controller can adapt measurement and feedback actions using only past measurement outcomes, enabling experiment-compatible quantum state preparation under partial observability.
engineering_relevance: The approach removes the need for full quantum-state knowledge and uses one-shot measurement-based rewards, making it more practical for scalable hardware experiments.
method: Use history of experimentally accessible measurement outcomes as the policy input.
Select both measurement operators and feedback actions in real time via reinforcement learning.
Train with a stochastic terminal reward from randomly sampled Hamiltonian components to estimate target energy unbiasedly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful demonstrations on ground-state preparation for the Bose-Hubbard model and GHZ state generation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of partial observations and the efficiency of the stochastic reward, which could become challenging in noisy or large-scale experiments.
paper_title: Experiment-compatible measurement--feedback quantum state preparation with reinforcement learning
